claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
A 1–5 μm alumina-based coating can be deposited on cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr by PVD or a similar technique.
The proposed deposition technique can provide high coating adherence and thermal stability.
The coating will form a continuous, adherent, dense oxide barrier.
The dense coating barrier will resist oxygen diffusion into the HfNbTaTiZr substrate at high temperature.
Restricting oxygen penetration will inhibit subsequent oxidation of the alloy surface.
The alumina-based coating will significantly improve the alloy's oxygen resistance around 1000 °C in air for exposures up to 100 hours.
The coated alloy will have substantially lower oxidation depth than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coated alloy will have substantially lower oxidation-related weight gain than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will preserve the alloy's room-temperature tensile ductility within its useful range.
The coating will preserve the alloy's 1000 °C yield strength within its useful range under strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
Coating thickness, composition, and deposition method may affect mechanical properties or introduce failure modes under cyclic thermal loading.
